stem: A city reports that it has planted many trees and that average surface temperatures have fallen. Which conclusion is most consistent with the passage?
options: The programme has probably reduced heat exposure equally, since both planting and temperature figures improved.
The figures alone cannot establish whether the most heat-exposed residents gained meaningful shade.
The lower surface temperatures show that tree survival and maintenance are no longer important concerns.
The city should disregard satellite data and rely exclusively on residents’ accounts of the heat.

verdicts.working: Planting totals and average surface temperatures do not show whether trees survived, where shade was created, or whether the most exposed residents benefited. Thus (B) is supported.

working: Planting totals do not show whether trees survive or where shade falls; average surface temperatures also differ from human exposure. The passage therefore says these figures alone may conceal who benefits.
solution: Planting totals and average surface temperatures do not show whether trees survive or whether shade reaches the most heat-exposed residents. Thus, the figures alone cannot establish who benefited.
